title: OpenCode Go is now a LiteLLM provider | liteLLM
summary: Use your OpenCode Go subscription through LiteLLM. Connect once, route models to the right API, preserve sessions, and track estimated usage.
body_markdown:
02


GET STARTED


## From a Go account to a first reply.


You need an active Go or Go Plus subscription and an API key from[OpenCode Console](https://opencode.ai/console) . The Console key authenticates LiteLLM to Go; signing in to the OpenCode app alone does not authenticate your gateway.


01


### Install and set your keys


Run these commands in the shell that will host LiteLLM. Replace the placeholders with your Console key and a long, random gateway key.


The OpenCode key stays on the gateway. Clients use the LiteLLM key.


Terminal


```text
pip install --upgrade 'litellm[proxy]'    export OPENCODE_API_KEY="your-opencode-api-key"    export LITELLM_MASTER_KEY="your-litellm-gateway-key"
```


02


### Add a Go model


Save this as` config.yaml` . The client calls the alias` go` ; LiteLLM calls the configured Go model. You do not need to set an upstream base URL.


For an existing gateway, add the model entry to your current configuration and keep your existing authentication settings.


config.yaml


```text
model_list  :         -     model_name  :   go          litellm_params  :             model  :   opencode_go/glm  -  5.3  -  flash            api_key  :   os.environ/OPENCODE_API_KEY        general_settings  :         master_key  :   os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
```


Start the local gateway


```text
litellm --config config.yaml --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4000
```


03


### Send a request


In another terminal, set the same` LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` and run this request.


A successful response contains a greeting in` choices\[0\].message.content` and token counts in` usage` . Reuse the session ID for later turns in this conversation.


First request


```text
curl http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \      -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \      -H 'x-litellm-session-id: go-demo' \      -d '{        "model": "go",        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello."}]      }'
```


04


### Connect the OpenCode app


With[OpenCode installed](https://opencode.ai/docs/) , add this to your project’s` opencode.json` , or merge the entry into its existing` provider` object.


Start` opencode` from that project in a shell with your gateway key set. Run` /models` , choose **Go · GLM-5.3-Flash** under **LiteLLM Go** , and send a message.


OpenCode talks to your local LiteLLM gateway. LiteLLM sends the request to Go.


opencode.json


```text
{         "$schema"  :     "https://opencode.ai/config.json"  ,         "provider"  :     {           "litellm-go"  :     {             "npm"  :     "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible"  ,             "name"  :     "LiteLLM Go"  ,             "options"  :     {               "baseURL"  :     "http://localhost:4000/v1"  ,               "apiKey"  :     "{env:LITELLM_MASTER_KEY}"             }  ,             "models"  :     {               "go"  :     {  "name"  :     "Go · GLM-5.3-Flash"  }             }           }         }      }
```
